title: Assistive Partner Responding to PwD Queries - Functional Test Plan
overview: Comprehensive functional testing of the AP Responding to PwD Queries feature on the Y4J AT/AD Vendor Portal. Covers Queries section access and visibility (summary counts, product-scoped queries), query listing with status indicators (Pending Response, Responded, Admin Response), responding to queries (single response per query, minimum word count, Pending Admin Approval), admin moderation workflow (approve, reject with reason, respond on behalf), approved response visibility and labeling, admin responses on behalf of vendor, privacy constraints (no chat threads, no PwD moderation, vendor moderation required), user feedback and notifications (new queries, approval/rejection alerts, notification counts).

inScope: Queries section access from AP dashboard navigation
Summary counts: Total Queries, Pending Responses, Responded Queries
Product-scoped visibility: only AP's own product queries shown
Query visibility restricted to PwD user, AP, and Admin
Query listing: product name/image, PwD user name, date/time, query text, status
Query statuses: Pending Response, Responded, Admin Response
Filter by status, search by product/user name/keyword
Response input enabled only for Pending Response status
Minimum word count requirement for responses
Pending Admin Approval status after submission
Admin moderation: Approve, Reject with reason, Respond on behalf
Rejection notification to AP with reason
Query returns to Pending Response on rejection for re-submission
Approved response labeled 'Your Response (Approved)' and visible to PwD
Admin Response labeled 'Admin Response (on your behalf)'
No chat/thread per query (single response only)
Notification counts for new queries, approvals, rejections

linkedIssues.summary: Admin Response status filter is not working in Queries tab

subtasks.summary: SD: Assistive Partner Responding to PwD Queries
Design: Assistive Partner Responding to PwD Queries

testCases.title: Verify Queries section is accessible from AP dashboard navigation
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as an approved Assistive Partner with listed products
steps: 1. Log in as an approved Assistive Partner
2. Navigate to the AP dashboard
3. Verify 'Queries' section is visible in the dashboard navigation
4. Click on the 'Queries' section
5. Verify the Queries page loads without errors
expectedResults: Queries section is visible in dashboard navigation
Clicking navigates to the Queries page
Page loads without console errors or broken UI
testCases.postconditions: User is on the Queries page

testCases.title: Verify summary counts display Total Queries, Pending Responses, and Responded Queries
testCases.preconditions: AP has products with queries in various statuses
steps: 1. Navigate to Queries section
2. Verify 'Total Queries' count is displayed
3. Verify 'Pending Responses' count is displayed
4. Verify 'Responded Queries' count is displayed
5. Verify the sum of Pending + Responded equals Total (or accounts for Admin Response)
6. Verify counts are accurate against actual query data
expectedResults: All three summary counts are displayed prominently
Total Queries count is accurate
Pending Responses count matches queries awaiting AP response
Responded Queries count matches queries with approved responses
testCases.postconditions: Summary counts are correctly displayed

testCases.title: Verify only queries related to AP's own products are visible
testCases.preconditions: Multiple APs exist with different products; PwDs have submitted queries for various products
steps: 1. Log in as Assistive Partner A
2. Navigate to Queries section
3. Verify only queries for AP A's products are displayed
4. Verify no queries for other APs' products are visible
5. Log out and log in as Assistive Partner B
6. Navigate to Queries section
7. Verify only queries for AP B's products are displayed
expectedResults: Each AP sees only queries for their own products
No cross-vendor query data is accessible
Data isolation is enforced
testCases.postconditions: Query visibility is scoped to AP's own products

testCases.title: Verify query listing displays all required fields with correct statuses
testCases.preconditions: AP has queries in different statuses (Pending Response, Responded, Admin Response)
steps: 1. Navigate to Queries section
2. Verify each query item displays:
a. Product name and image
b. PwD user name
c. Date and time of query
d. Query text
e. Current status
3. Verify status labels are correct:
a. 'Pending Response' for unanswered queries
b. 'Responded' for queries with approved AP responses
c. 'Admin Response' for queries answered by admin on behalf
4. Verify product images load correctly
expectedResults: All required fields are displayed for each query
Status labels are accurate and visually distinct
Product images load correctly
Date/time format is readable
testCases.postconditions: Query listing displays complete data

testCases.title: Verify queries can be filtered by status
testCases.preconditions: AP has queries in multiple statuses
steps: 1. Navigate to Queries section
2. Locate the status filter
3. Filter by 'Pending Response'
4. Verify only Pending Response queries are shown
5. Filter by 'Responded'
6. Verify only Responded queries are shown
7. Filter by 'Admin Response'
8. Verify only Admin Response queries are shown
9. Clear all filters
10. Verify all queries are displayed
expectedResults: Status filter is available with all status options
Filtering by each status shows only matching queries
Clearing filters restores the full list
Filter updates are instant without page reload
testCases.postconditions: Status filter works correctly

testCases.title: Verify queries can be searched by product, user name, or keyword
testCases.preconditions: AP has multiple queries with different products and users
steps: 1. Navigate to Queries section
2. Search by product name
3. Verify results show only queries for that product
4. Clear search and search by PwD user name
5. Verify results show only queries from that user
6. Clear search and search by a keyword from query text
7. Verify results show queries containing that keyword
8. Clear search
9. Verify all queries are restored
expectedResults: Search by product name returns matching queries
Search by user name returns matching queries
Search by keyword returns queries containing the keyword
Clearing search restores the full list
testCases.postconditions: Search functionality works correctly

testCases.title: Verify AP can submit a response to a Pending Response query
testCases.preconditions: AP has a query with 'Pending Response' status
steps: 1. Navigate to Queries section
2. Locate a query with 'Pending Response' status
3. Verify a response input field is enabled
4. Enter a response meeting the minimum word count requirement
5. Submit the response
6. Verify a success confirmation is shown
7. Verify the response status changes to 'Pending Admin Approval'
8. Verify the response is NOT visible to the PwD user yet
expectedResults: Response input is enabled for Pending Response queries
Response can be entered and submitted
Status changes to 'Pending Admin Approval' after submission
Response is not visible to PwD until admin approval
testCases.postconditions: Response is submitted and awaiting admin approval

testCases.title: Verify only one response per query is allowed
testCases.preconditions: AP has already submitted a response for a query (in Pending Admin Approval or Approved status)
steps: 1. Navigate to a query that already has an AP response submitted
2. Verify the response input field is disabled or hidden
3. Verify no 'Respond' button is available
4. Verify a message or indicator shows the response has been submitted
expectedResults: Response input is disabled after a response has been submitted
AP cannot submit a second response to the same query
Clear indication that a response already exists
testCases.postconditions: Single response restriction is enforced

testCases.title: Verify response input is disabled for non-Pending Response queries
testCases.preconditions: AP has queries in 'Responded' and 'Admin Response' statuses
steps: 1. Navigate to a query with 'Responded' status
2. Verify response input is disabled or not shown
3. Navigate to a query with 'Admin Response' status
4. Verify response input is disabled or not shown
5. Navigate to a query with 'Pending Response' status
6. Verify response input IS enabled
expectedResults: Response input is disabled for 'Responded' queries
Response input is disabled for 'Admin Response' queries
Response input is enabled only for 'Pending Response' queries
testCases.postconditions: Response input availability matches query status

testCases.title: Verify minimum word count requirement is enforced before submission
testCases.preconditions: AP is responding to a Pending Response query
steps: 1. Open response input for a Pending Response query
2. Enter text below the minimum word count
3. Attempt to submit
4. Verify a validation error is displayed indicating minimum word count not met
5. Enter text meeting the minimum word count
6. Attempt to submit
7. Verify submission is successful
expectedResults: Submission is blocked when word count is below minimum
Clear validation message indicates the minimum requirement
Submission succeeds when minimum word count is met
testCases.postconditions: Minimum word count is enforced

testCases.title: Verify AP cannot submit an empty response
testCases.preconditions: AP is responding to a Pending Response query
steps: 1. Open response input for a Pending Response query
2. Leave the response field empty
3. Attempt to submit
4. Verify submission is blocked with a validation error
5. Enter only whitespace
6. Attempt to submit
7. Verify submission is blocked
expectedResults: Empty response cannot be submitted
Whitespace-only response cannot be submitted
Clear validation message is displayed
testCases.postconditions: Empty responses are prevented

testCases.title: Verify admin can approve AP response making it visible to PwD user
testCases.preconditions: AP has submitted a response in 'Pending Admin Approval' status
steps: 1. Log in as admin
2. Navigate to the moderation queue
3. Locate the AP's pending response
4. Click 'Approve'
5. Verify the response status changes to 'Approved'
6. Log in as the PwD user who submitted the query
7. Verify the AP response is now visible to the PwD user
8. Verify the response is labeled appropriately
expectedResults: Admin can approve the AP response
Response becomes visible to the PwD user after approval
Query status updates to 'Responded'
Response is labeled 'Your Response (Approved)' for the AP
testCases.postconditions: Response is approved and visible to PwD

testCases.title: Verify admin can reject AP response with a clear rejection reason
testCases.preconditions: AP has submitted a response in 'Pending Admin Approval' status
steps: 1. Log in as admin
2. Navigate to the moderation queue
3. Locate the AP's pending response
4. Click 'Reject'
5. Enter a clear rejection reason
6. Submit the rejection
7. Verify the query returns to 'Pending Response' status
8. Log in as the AP
9. Verify the AP can view the rejection reason
10. Verify a notification is sent to the AP with the rejection reason
expectedResults: Admin can reject with a reason
Query returns to 'Pending Response' status for re-submission
AP can view the rejection reason
Notification is sent to AP with the reason
testCases.postconditions: Response is rejected; AP can re-submit

testCases.title: Verify admin can submit a response on behalf of the Assistive Partner
testCases.preconditions: A query exists with 'Pending Response' status
steps: 1. Log in as admin
2. Navigate to the query in Pending Response status
3. Submit a response on behalf of the Assistive Partner
4. Verify the response is saved successfully
5. Log in as the AP
6. Navigate to the query
7. Verify the response is labeled 'Admin Response (on your behalf)'
8. Verify the query status is 'Responded'
9. Verify the AP cannot add a separate response
10. Log in as PwD user
11. Verify the response is visible to the PwD user
expectedResults: Admin can respond on behalf of the AP
Response is labeled 'Admin Response (on your behalf)' for the AP
Query status changes to 'Responded'
AP cannot submit a separate response after admin responds
Response is visible to the PwD user
testCases.postconditions: Admin response on behalf is published

testCases.title: Verify AP can re-submit response after rejection
testCases.preconditions: AP's response was rejected; query is back in 'Pending Response' status
steps: 1. Log in as AP
2. Navigate to the rejected query (now in 'Pending Response' status)
3. Verify the rejection reason is visible
4. Verify the response input is enabled again
5. Enter a new response addressing the rejection feedback
6. Submit the new response
7. Verify the status changes to 'Pending Admin Approval'
expectedResults: Response input is re-enabled after rejection
Rejection reason is visible to help AP improve response
New response can be submitted
Status returns to 'Pending Admin Approval'
testCases.postconditions: Re-submitted response awaits admin approval

testCases.title: Verify approved response is labeled 'Your Response (Approved)' and visible to PwD
testCases.preconditions: AP response has been approved by admin
steps: 1. Log in as the AP
2. Navigate to the query with approved response
3. Verify the response is labeled 'Your Response (Approved)'
4. Verify the query status shows 'Responded'
5. Log in as the PwD user
6. Navigate to the product/query
7. Verify the AP response content is visible to the PwD user
expectedResults: Response is labeled 'Your Response (Approved)' for the AP
Query status is 'Responded'
Response content is visible to the PwD user
Response content matches what was submitted
testCases.postconditions: Approved response is correctly displayed to both AP and PwD

testCases.title: Verify AP cannot edit or submit another response after approval
testCases.preconditions: AP response has been approved
steps: 1. Log in as AP
2. Navigate to the query with approved response
3. Verify no 'Edit' button is available on the approved response
4. Verify no 'Respond' or 'Submit' button is available
5. Verify the response is read-only
expectedResults: No edit functionality is available after approval
No option to submit another response
Response is displayed as read-only
testCases.postconditions: Approved response is immutable

testCases.title: Verify Admin Response on behalf is labeled correctly and blocks AP response
testCases.category: 6. Admin Responses on Behalf of Vendor
testCases.preconditions: Admin has responded on behalf of the AP
steps: 1. Log in as the AP
2. Navigate to the query where admin responded on behalf
3. Verify the response is labeled 'Admin Response (on your behalf)'
4. Verify the query status is 'Responded'
5. Verify no response input is available for the AP
6. Verify the AP cannot add a separate response
expectedResults: Response is clearly labeled 'Admin Response (on your behalf)'
Query status shows 'Responded'
AP cannot submit a separate response
Response input is disabled/hidden
testCases.postconditions: Admin response blocks further AP responses

testCases.title: Verify no chat or back-and-forth thread is allowed per query
testCases.preconditions: Query has an approved response
steps: 1. Log in as PwD user
2. Navigate to the query with an approved AP response
3. Verify no 'Reply' or 'Follow-up' option is available
4. Log in as AP
5. Navigate to the same query
6. Verify no option to add additional responses or comments
7. Verify the interaction is limited to: one query + one response
expectedResults: No reply/follow-up option for PwD after response
No additional response option for AP after approval
Interaction is strictly one query + one response
No chat thread functionality exists
testCases.postconditions: Single-response constraint is enforced

testCases.title: Verify PwD queries do not require moderation
testCases.preconditions: PwD user submits a new query on a product
steps: 1. Have a PwD user submit a query on an AP's product
2. Log in as the AP
3. Navigate to Queries section
4. Verify the new query is immediately visible to the AP
5. Verify the query did not go through any moderation queue
6. Verify the query status is 'Pending Response'
expectedResults: PwD queries appear immediately without moderation
Query is visible to AP right after submission
Status is 'Pending Response' immediately
testCases.postconditions: PwD queries are unmoderated and immediately visible

testCases.title: Verify all responses and moderation actions are logged for audit
testCases.preconditions: Multiple query responses have been submitted, approved, and rejected
steps: 1. Submit a response as AP
2. Have admin approve it
3. Submit another response for a different query
4. Have admin reject it
5. Verify audit logs contain all actions with timestamps
6. Verify logs include: submission, approval, rejection actions
expectedResults: All response submissions are logged with timestamps
All moderation actions (approve/reject) are logged
Audit trail is complete and chronological
testCases.postconditions: Audit trail exists for all query interactions

testCases.title: Verify AP receives notification when a new query is received
testCases.preconditions: PwD user submits a new query for AP's product
steps: 1. Have a PwD user submit a new query for an AP's product
2. Log in as the AP
3. Verify a notification appears indicating a new query
4. Verify the notification count updates
5. Click the notification
6. Verify navigation to the new query
expectedResults: Notification appears for new query
Notification count increments
Clicking notification navigates to the query
testCases.postconditions: AP is aware of the new query

testCases.title: Verify AP receives notification when response is approved
testCases.preconditions: AP has submitted a response; admin approves it
steps: 1. Submit a response as AP
2. Have admin approve the response
3. Log in as the AP
4. Verify a notification appears indicating approval
5. Verify the notification count updates
6. Verify clear visual indicator for 'Approved' status on the query
expectedResults: Approval notification appears on AP dashboard
Notification count updates
Clear visual indicator shows approved status
testCases.postconditions: AP is informed of approval

testCases.title: Verify AP receives notification when response is rejected with reason
testCases.preconditions: AP has submitted a response; admin rejects it with a reason
steps: 1. Submit a response as AP
2. Have admin reject the response with a reason
3. Log in as the AP
4. Verify a notification appears indicating rejection
5. Verify the notification includes or links to the rejection reason
6. Verify the notification count updates
7. Verify clear visual indicator for 'Rejected' status with reason visible
expectedResults: Rejection notification appears on AP dashboard
Notification includes/links to the rejection reason
Notification count updates
Clear visual indicator shows rejected status with reason
testCases.postconditions: AP is informed of rejection with actionable feedback

testCases.title: Verify visual indicators for Pending Admin Approval, Approved, and Rejected statuses
testCases.preconditions: AP has queries/responses in all three moderation states
steps: 1. Navigate to Queries section
2. Locate a query with response in 'Pending Admin Approval'
3. Verify a clear visual indicator (badge, color, icon) shows pending status
4. Locate a query with 'Approved' response
5. Verify a clear visual indicator shows approved status
6. Locate a query with 'Rejected' response
7. Verify a clear visual indicator shows rejected status with reason accessible
expectedResults: Pending Admin Approval has a distinct visual indicator
Approved responses have a distinct visual indicator
Rejected responses have a distinct visual indicator
All indicators are clearly distinguishable from each other
testCases.postconditions: Visual feedback is clear for all moderation states

testCases.title: Verify queries section with zero queries shows appropriate empty state
testCases.preconditions: AP has products but no PwD queries have been submitted
steps: 1. Log in as AP with no queries
2. Navigate to Queries section
3. Verify the page loads without errors
4. Verify summary counts show 0 for all metrics
5. Verify an appropriate empty state message is displayed
6. Verify no broken UI elements
expectedResults: Page loads successfully with zero queries
Summary counts show 0
Empty state message is displayed (e.g., 'No queries received yet')
UI is clean with no broken elements
testCases.postconditions: Empty state is handled gracefully

testCases.title: Verify Admin Response status filter works correctly
testCases.preconditions: AP has queries with 'Admin Response' status (admin responded on behalf)
steps: 1. Navigate to Queries section
2. Locate the status filter
3. Select 'Admin Response' filter
4. Verify only queries with Admin Response status are shown
5. Verify the filter returns correct results
6. Verify no other status queries are included
expectedResults: Admin Response filter option is available
Filtering shows only Admin Response queries
Results are accurate and complete
No false positives from other statuses
testCases.postconditions: Admin Response filter works correctly (regression for SCRUM-863)
